scope: why the read path runs once

chain.0x4FEA90: call 0x4FE220 (unconditional in the frame driver; only 0x49DF20 is conditionally skipped before it)

finding: the call from 0x4FEA90 to 0x4FE220 has no condition guarding it, so the read path runs whenever the frame driver runs. Since the read-packet breakpoint fires only once, the frame driver itself runs only once (or only one of its callers fires once).

top_loop.note: the call to the frame driver is unconditional in the loop body; the only jumps into 0x77FA64 come from 0x77FA2A and 0x77FA33, which skip earlier bookkeeping, not the driver call itself

breakpoint_caveat: the launcher's breakpoints may be one-shot (removed after the first hit). If so, '1 hit' only proves 'called at least once' and the real evidence is that recv_helper had ZERO hits, which is reliable.
refined_conclusion: the frame driver runs every frame, and 0x5C2260 is reached every frame, but 0x674EB0 is never called -- so 0x5C2260 must return early before 0x5C2380. Its early exits are: [0x84abb08]/[0x84abb14] setup, 0x5C22B5 (msg length < 4), 0x5C22FC (phase < 7), 0x5C2315 (msg length < 4 again).
